terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: Argus is an early access product for educational investing research. These terms describe how Argus works today. Argus is still being built, so these terms will change as the product does.

no_investment_advice.title: No investment advice
no_investment_advice.body: Argus provides educational tools that help you structure and review investing ideas. Argus does not provide investment, legal, tax, accounting, or financial advice. You are responsible for your own decisions.

no_brokerage.title: No brokerage or trading relationship
no_brokerage.body: Argus is not a broker, dealer, investment adviser, fiduciary, exchange, custodian, or trading venue. Argus does not hold funds, place orders, execute trades, or connect to brokerage accounts.

historical_simulations.title: Historical simulations are hypothetical
historical_simulations.body: Historical simulations are hypothetical and depend on the assumptions, data availability, asset support, benchmark defaults, and time windows shown in the product. Simulated returns are not guarantees of future performance.

early_access_changes.title: Early access availability and changes
early_access_changes.body: Argus is in early access and is provided as is, without warranties. Features may change, break, reset, or be removed without notice, and some may never reach a full release. We may limit access, suspend accounts, or remove content that creates security, abuse, compliance, or operational risk.

eligibility.title: Eligibility
eligibility.body: You must be old enough to form a binding agreement in your jurisdiction and allowed to use Argus under applicable law. Do not use Argus on behalf of another person or organization unless you are authorized to do so.

acceptable_use.title: Acceptable use
acceptable_use.body: Do not use Argus to break the law, abuse the service, reverse engineer private systems, overload providers, submit sensitive third-party data, or present generated output as professional advice.

third_party_services.title: Third-party services
third_party_services.body: Argus relies on third-party services for hosting, authentication, market data, model access, bot protection, and chart rendering. TradingView Lightweight Charts is used for chart rendering and attribution, not as an Argus market data source.

account_support.title: Account support
account_support.body_before_email: While Argus is in early access, account deletion and support requests are handled by a person. Contact
account_support.body_after_email: or use the in-app account deletion request.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what Argus does with your account data, conversations, feedback, and the requests it sends to outside providers while the product is in early access.

data_collect.title: Data we collect
data_collect.body: Argus may collect account details, authentication state, conversations, investing ideas you submit, saved product records, feedback, support requests, browser and device basics, usage events, logs, and error diagnostics.

data_use.title: How we use data
data_use.body: We use data to run the product, authenticate users, save and restore conversations, generate and review historical simulations, debug failures, protect the service, respond to support, and improve Argus while it is in early access.

ai_market_data.title: AI and market data providers
ai_market_data.body: Conversation content and prompts may be sent to OpenRouter and model providers so Argus can interpret requests and draft responses. Market data and asset discovery may use providers such as Alpaca and Kraken. Provider availability can affect supported symbols, time windows, and results.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure and product services
infrastructure.body: Argus uses Supabase for authentication and product persistence, Render for hosting, OpenRouter for model access, and Cloudflare for domain delivery and bot protection. Product analytics through PostHog run on Argus servers, and only when they are intentionally enabled. TradingView Lightweight Charts is used as a charting library with attribution; it is not the source of Argus market data.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: Argus stores a small amount of data in your browser. All of it either keeps the product working or remembers your settings, and none of it is advertising or tracking, which is why Argus does not show a cookie consent banner.

sign_in.label: Sign-in cookies
sign_in.body: These keep you signed in as you move between pages. Supabase authentication sets them, and Argus refreshes them while you keep using the product. They stay after you close the browser, and signing out clears them. Signing in or resetting your password also sets a short-lived cookie that completes the exchange securely, discarded once it finishes. If you block them, signing in will not work.

guest_handoff.label: Guest handoff cookies
guest_handoff.body: If you start as a guest and then create an account, Argus sets two cookies so your temporary conversation can move onto the new account. Signing in to an account you already have uses a ten minute cookie. Creating a new account uses one that lasts as long as your guest workspace, up to seven days. Both are limited to Argus authentication routes, travel to the Argus API on its own domain, and are cleared as soon as the handoff finishes.

security.label: Security cookies
security.body: Cloudflare Turnstile checks that sign-in and guest requests come from a person rather than a bot, and Cloudflare may set short-lived challenge cookies to do that. They are scoped to Argus and are not used to follow you across other sites.

preferences.label: Preferences you set
preferences.body: Your browser’s local storage holds your language, which starts from your browser’s own setting until you change it, along with your appearance and layout choices, tips you dismissed, the conversations you marked temporary, and the ad or link that brought you here. Language, appearance, layout, tips, and temporary-chat marks stay on your device. The campaign is stored there too, and Argus may receive it when you start as a guest or create an account. This tab temporarily keeps your account identifier, the daily-limit reset time, and whether you closed the notice. That notice state clears when the limit resets, a question succeeds, you sign out or switch accounts, or you close the tab. Argus never sends any of this to advertisers.

cookies.body_after: Argus does not use advertising cookies, ad pixels, marketing trackers, or cross-site tracking, and it does not share browser data with advertising partners. Product analytics, when enabled, run on Argus servers and store nothing in your browser. You can clear or block this storage in your browser settings, though signing in will stop working if you block the sign-in cookies.

access_retention.title: Access and retention
access_retention.body: Founder and administrator access is limited to operating, debugging, securing, and improving Argus during early access. We keep data while your account is active, while needed for support or security, or while required by operational records.

your_controls.title: Your controls
your_controls.body_before_email: You can archive or delete conversations in the app. While Argus is in early access, account deletion is handled by a person through the in-app request or by contacting

sale_personal_info.title: Sale and sharing of personal information
sale_personal_info.body: Argus does not sell or share your personal information, and it does not use it for targeted advertising. If that ever changes, this policy and the controls in the product will be updated before it takes effect.
